aggressive_definition: Advanced-stage prostate cancer, with no stage criteria provided in the abstract.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: After an average of 8.7 years of follow-up, there were 2727 incident cases of prostate cancer, of which 1131 were known to be localised and 541 advanced-stage disease.
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition using Cox regression.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We examined consumption of animal foods, protein and calcium in relation to risk of prostate cancer among 142 251 men in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
reason: The abstract reports total incident prostate cancer associations and describes the number of advanced-stage cases, but it does not report or otherwise establish an exposure association analysis for advanced-stage disease. A stage count alone does not establish an aggressive endpoint analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: After an average of 8.7 years of follow-up, there were 2727 incident cases of prostate cancer, of which 1131 were known to be localised and 541 advanced-stage disease.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied calcium estimate is explicitly identified in existing evidence as an incident prostate cancer estimate. The abstract supports the general incident endpoint but does not establish that this estimate concerns advanced-stage disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: A high intake of dairy protein was associated with an increased risk, with a hazard ratio for the top versus the bottom fifth of intake of 1.22 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-1.41, P(trend)=0.02).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported dairy-protein hazard ratio is for prostate cancer overall; it is not identified as an advanced-stage estimate.
